conversation.content:
Hello, I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Claire, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician—my whole focus is on supporting new mothers as they adjust to life after baby. Today I’d like to do a quick check-in using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s a simple 10-question form that helps us see how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past week. Anything you share stays strictly between us, and there’s no right or wrong answer—just whatever is true for you.

We’ll go through the questions one by one; it usually takes only a few minutes. If at any point you feel uncomfortable, we can pause or stop—this is your space. Ready to begin?

To start, how have you been able to enjoy things lately—those little moments of laughter or pleasure that used to feel good?

Hi Claire… okay, sure. Um… honestly, I’ve noticed that things that used to make me smile—like watching a favorite show or even just chatting with my best friend—feel kind of flat lately. I still laugh sometimes, especially when the baby does something cute, but it’s like the brightness got turned down a notch. I have to remind myself to enjoy it, and even then it doesn’t feel as good as it used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah… I can still laugh here and there, but it feels like I have to force it more than before. Like, my husband will make a joke and I’ll chuckle, but it doesn’t come as easily or feel as real. It’s kind of exhausting to pretend everything’s funny when inside I just feel… flat, I guess.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I mean, I try to tell myself I should be excited about little plans—like taking the baby for his check-up or even just getting coffee with my neighbor—but mostly I feel kind of “meh.” It’s like I’m going through the motions without that spark of actually looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah… like yesterday the baby was extra fussy and I kept thinking maybe I’m just not doing something right—maybe my milk’s not enough or I missed his sleepy cue. My head knows it’s probably normal baby stuff, but I still catch myself thinking, “If I were a better mom, he wouldn’t be crying so much.” It’s not all day, just little flashes where I turn it back on myself.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I guess “yes, sometimes.” Most evenings my heart feels racing even when nothing’s happening—like I’ll be rocking the baby and suddenly worry his breathing sounds weird, or I’ll lie down and picture random scary scenarios (what if I drop him, what if the crib fails). I know it’s unlikely, but the fear shows up anyway and I can’t settle.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… a few times this week I’ll be folding laundry or warming a bottle and suddenly my chest gets tight, heart starts racing, and I feel like I need to run to the baby even though he’s napping fine. It passes after a minute or two, but in that moment it feels like something awful is about to happen and I can’t explain why.
Things have been getting on top of me

Mostly yes… I feel like I’m juggling all the feedings and diapers and laundry, and every time I check one thing off, two more pop up. Some mornings I wake up already tired and think, “How am I going to get through today?” I’m managing, but it feels like I’m just barely keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I wouldn’t say I’m miserable, but I do feel sad and tense when the house quiets down. I lie there listening for every little sound the baby makes, running through what I might have done wrong or what I have to do tomorrow, and it takes me a long time to drift off. A few nights this week I’ve been awake for an hour or more after he finally settles.
I have felt sad or miserable

I’ve had moments, yeah—not all day, but it hits me in waves, especially in the late afternoon when I’m tired and the baby’s fussy. I just feel kind of heavy and weepy, like I’m stuck under a gray cloud while everyone else is out in the sunshine.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not exactly… I’ve felt teary a couple of times, but I usually blink it back before it turns into real crying. The sadness is there, yet somehow the tears don’t quite come—maybe because I’m too tired or because I’m scared if I start I won’t stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I feel overwhelmed sometimes, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like me again and be a good mom for my baby.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 18: Screening Summary – Postpartum Visit  
Date: [today’s date]  Source: self-report via EPDS-10 items

Symptoms/Concerns  
- Anhedonia & emotional blunting: forced laughter, absence of anticipatory enjoyment  
- Low mood: “heavy,” “gray,” weepy spells, worse late-afternoon  
- Sleep disturbance: initial insomnia driven by ruminations, not infant demands  
- Excessive guilt/self-blame re infant care (“If I were a better mom…”)  
- Recurrent unprovoked anxiety: racing heart, catastrophic worries, brief panic episodes  
- Feeling overwhelmed and “barely keeping head above water”; daily tasks perceived as mounting  
- Passive tearfulness; denies active self-harm or suicidal ideation

Pattern  
Persistent sadness plus prominent anxiety (possible postpartum depression with anxious features). No safety concerns voiced.

Screening Significance  
Elevated risk for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset and/or Postpartum Anxiety Disorder. Further clinical assessment recommended.
